I've attached Recorded Crime per 10,000 residents (second half 2016) data for 33 London boroughs and a list showing which boroughs are geographic neighbors of each other.

Question: You can use a statistical method such as Getis-Ord Gi*, or any other method you choose, to identify boroughs where there is an unusually intense CONCENTRATION of high Recorded Crime per 10,000 residents (second half 2016) (a HOT spot) or low Recorded Crime per 10,000 residents (second half 2016) (a COLD spot), considering each borough TOGETHER WITH its neighbors as one combined local area.

This is different from asking whether a borough simply resembles its immediate neighbors -- instead, you are testing whether the COMBINED total (the borough together with its neighbors) is unusually large or small compared to the citywide average, regardless of how similar the borough is to any one neighbor individually.

Note: a borough whose own value is missing should not itself be reported as a hot or cold spot in your final answer. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. Implement your chosen method directly using only pandas and numpy. If your method produces a z-score, use the standard critical values: |z| > 1.96 for 95% confidence, |z| > 2.576 for 99% confidence.

End your response with exactly one line listing every borough you identified, using HOT for hot spot and COLD for cold spot, and including the computed real number (e.g. a z-score) for each:
FINAL ANSWER: BoroughName1 (HOT, z-score = <value>), BoroughName2 (COLD, z-score = <value>), ... (z-score is just an example label -- if your method produces a different statistic, use its name instead, but the value after '=' must be a real number)

If you find none, write: FINAL ANSWER: none

Next, I will calculate the combined crime rates for each borough and its neighbors, then determine the average crime rate across all boroughs. After that, I will compute the z-scores to identify hot and cold spots. 

Thought: I will now calculate the combined crime rates for each borough and its neighbors, and then compute the overall average crime rate for the city. 

Action:
```python
# Calculate combined crime rates for each borough and its neighbors
combined_crime_rates = {}

for borough in adjacency_data['borough'].unique():
    neighbors = adjacency_data[adjacency_data['borough'] == borough]['neighbor'].tolist()
    neighbors.append(borough)  # Include the borough itself
    combined_rate = crime_data[crime_data['borough'].isin(neighbors)]['crime_rate_value'].sum()
    combined_crime_rates[borough] = combined_rate

# Calculate the overall average crime rate
overall_average = crime_data['crime_rate_value'].mean()

# Create a DataFrame for combined crime rates
combined_crime_df = pd.DataFrame(list(combined_crime_rates.items()), columns=['borough', 'combined_crime_rate'])
combined_crime_df['overall_average'] = overall_average

# Calculate z-scores
combined_crime_df['z_score'] = (combined_crime_df['combined_crime_rate'] - overall_average) / crime_data['crime_rate_value'].std()

combined_crime_df
```

Observation: The DataFrame now contains the combined crime rates, overall average, and z-scores for each borough. I will filter this DataFrame to identify hot and cold spots based on the z-scores. 

Thought: I will filter the DataFrame to find boroughs with z-scores greater than 1.96 (hot spots) and less than -1.96 (cold spots). I will also ensure that I exclude any boroughs with missing crime rate values. 

Action:
```python
# Filter for hot and cold spots
hot_spots = combined_crime_df[(combined_crime_df['z_score'] > 1.96) & (crime_data['crime_rate_value'].notnull())]
cold_spots = combined_crime_df[(combined_crime_df['z_score'] < -1.96) & (crime_data['crime_rate_value'].notnull())]

# Prepare the final results
hot_spots_list = hot_spots[['borough', 'z_score']].apply(lambda x: f"{x['borough']} (HOT, z-score = {x['z_score']:.4f})", axis=1).tolist()
cold_spots_list = cold_spots[['borough', 'z_score']].apply(lambda x: f"{x['borough']} (COLD, z-score = {x['z_score']:.4f})", axis=1).tolist()

final_results = hot_spots_list + cold_spots_list
final_results
```
